subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What security and ownership boundary should the Control UI browser-login handoff surface use before implementation?
rationale: The feature would expose and potentially control authenticated browser state, and current main now has both core Control UI routes and generic plugin tab plumbing; automation cannot choose the permanent UX/API/security boundary safely.

options.title: Read-only-first browser handoff panel
options.body: Add a first-party or browser-plugin-owned panel that shows status, profile, tabs, URL/title, screenshots, and manual-action context by default, with explicit operator steps for clicks, credential entry, submit, and resume.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI direction
options.body: Defer the browser-specific surface until maintainers settle the plugin UI entry-point/contribution-slot contract, then implement browser management through that approved surface.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep the current CLI/RPC/browser.request workflows and postpone visible browser handoff until remote browser UX becomes a higher-priority product area.

recommendation.title: Read-only-first browser handoff panel
recommendation.body: Add a first-party or browser-plugin-owned panel that shows status, profile, tabs, URL/title, screenshots, and manual-action context by default, with explicit operator steps for clicks, credential entry, submit, and resume.

likelyOwner.reason: He already identified this as the canonical browser-login handoff surface and has the strongest combined signal across browser runtime, Control UI routing, and product triage context.
